releases.title: The rental shop, rebuilt around a busy Saturday: paid and ready to fit, signed fitting cards, guest forms, groups, scan-to-return, season rentals and card deposits

notes.text: Paid and ready to fit: a rental sold in Sell or online no longer needs gear chosen at payment. Each renter waits in Ready to fit on the Counter tab, found by name, phone, order number or a scanned receipt, and gear goes out from there. Handing out gear with nothing paid needs a manager and a reason.

A fitting card for each person: height, weight, date of birth, boot size, sole length, stance and how they ski (cautious, moderate or aggressive), saved to the customer, with the binding setting suggested from your chart using that person's details only. Settings are never copied from a past rental.

The renter signs on screen that their details are true before skis or a snowboard go out; a parent or guardian signs for anyone under 18. The signature, the details and the gear print on a rental agreement.
Shops with stations: each paid rental moves through Form, Boots, Ski tech and Door, each station sees its own queue with wait times, and a queue board shows the line on a wall screen.

The guest rental form: guests fill in each renter's sizes and ability on their phone and sign, from a link in their order email, a QR code on the receipt, or a QR poster in line. The Forms tab picks it up at the counter.
Groups: schools and clubs add members by list or a parents' link, gear is set aside the night before with bag labels, and the morning hand-out is one scan per bag.

Returns tab: scan each gear tag and it is checked in at once, with Damaged and Lost one tap away. Out now searches by name, phone, tag or contract and filters overdue, due today, groups and season rentals.

Card deposits: the deposit is held on the guest's card on the counter's card reader and let go when the gear comes back; fees can be taken from it once staff confirm. Longer and season rentals keep the card on file instead.
Season rentals: a rental product can be a season rental, due back on the shop's season return date, with reminder emails in March and when overdue, and a buy-out that sells the gear to the family.
Rental reports: use by piece, type and size, gear that rarely goes out, repair spend, fees charged, collected and waived, rental money per piece, and late returns.

One gear picker everywhere (Sell, the fitting card, groups), with counts by size and What's left; it loads the whole fleet, where lists used to stop at 500 pieces. Due back now defaults to the shop's closing time.

releases.title: Website: attractions and summer, who each plan is for, and the reason to switch said plainly

notes.text: Website: a new page for attractions and activities (ziplines, mountain coasters, tubing, skating) at /attraction-ticketing-software, in the Product menu, the sitemap and llms.txt.

Website home: the headline now reads Run the whole mountain from one screen, the morning board shows attractions, the day has an 11:00 AM attractions card, each plan says who it is for, and the patrol director's way in is a visible line under the buttons.
Website pricing: paying over the season is described as the yearly price in six payments, with nothing in the months between, and a new question answers which plan runs a summer operation.

Product page: Attractions, Activities by time slot, Patrol checklists you choose and Menus by role lead New this season, and an Attractions and activities block joins Operations. The Ski patrol page describes the checklists your patrol chooses.
Help, Coming to Verdynt/OS: summer operations now lists only what is left (a waiver per product, bike rentals, group and event bookings).
The Resort plan's line now reads Larger operations with a patrol, a terrain park and attractions to run, where it still had the launch wording.

releases.title: Demo-readiness fixes: the sale is checked before payment, quick sale by default, patrol with no signal, the privacy list

notes.text: A sale is checked before any money is taken. A missing waiver, a rider under the age limit, a lesson that has filled up or gear that is out is refused on the details step, never after the guest has paid or the card reader has charged their card.

A basket of day tickets, punch cards, vouchers or gift cards opens on the quick sale. Press Next: payment to sell with no name, or Add guest details to put the sale on a customer record. A quick-sale receipt line no longer starts with a stray comma.
A case started with no signal can name its trail, lift or attraction: the lists are kept on the phone while there is a signal.
Submit report is one check. Anything required is listed first, and the suggestions with Submit anyway appear only once everything required is in.
Me is the first choice when naming a responder. A patroller whose login has no staff record gets one on the patrol roster, linked to the login and written to the audit log.
With no signal, a case shows one strip, saying there is no signal and how many entries are waiting to send, in place of the banner, the note and the pop-up messages.
Settings, Team and logins: a username you type in Add login is kept. The suggestion from the email only fills the box while it is untouched. The Logins table stays inside its card on a wide screen.

The privacy policy lists every outside service Verdynt/OS sends information to, what each one receives and why, and promises to tell mountains before adding one. The Security page and the assistant's Help say what the assistant can and cannot see.

A guest's link to their signed waiver copy stops working when the season it was signed for ends, or twelve months after signing when no season end is set. Staff still open every signed copy from Waivers. The link's code is no longer kept in plain form in the database.
Dark theme: the Open and Closed buttons, gate results and other green and red fills read clearly, and the pricing page on a phone no longer draws the price over the plan description.

releases.title: Patrol checklists you choose, and attractions: ziplines, coasters, ice skating, tubing and more

notes.text: Patrol has 22 new checklists: cardiac arrest, chest pain, breathing trouble or allergic reaction, seizure, diabetic emergency, cold injury, fracture or dislocation, tree well, avalanche, lost person, terrain park, uphill traffic, an intoxicated guest, a death on the mountain, lift evacuation, and lists for ziplines, coasters, ice skating, tubing, scenic rides, the bike park, aerial parks and climbing walls.

Patrol admins choose which checklists their patrol sees, and write their own, under Settings, Patrol, Checklists. Preview any list before switching it on. A list of your own can suggest itself for cases at a kind of attraction.

Lists that fit a case show up by themselves, including the right list when the case happened at an attraction. Add a checklist offers every other list with one tap, and each row is a large target that works with gloves on.

A checklist tick always reads the way it was ticked, even if the list is renamed or switched off later. Ticks show in frozen copies and the claim file. With no signal, a tick waits on the phone and is sent with the time it was ticked.

Attractions: add your zipline, mountain coaster, tubing hill, ice rink, scenic ride, bike park, disc golf, aerial park, climbing wall or anything else under Settings, Attractions, with height, weight and age limits and whether a waiver is needed.
Each attraction has Open, On hold and Closed on Mountain status, like a lift. On hold asks why, and downtime is logged with a reason.

Daily opening inspections for attractions, ticked on a phone. A failed inspection closes the attraction and keeps it from opening until a new one passes. The checks start from defaults for each type; change them to match your manufacturer's manual and your state inspector.
Today's morning board and the wall screen show your attractions, and a failed inspection shows at the top.

A patrol case can name the attraction it happened at. The Activity list now includes zipline, mountain coaster, ice skating, scenic lift ride, mountain biking, disc golf, aerial park and climbing. Statistics and the season risk report count cases at each attraction.
Staff and schedule has an Attractions department, with suggested positions and certifications for each attraction, such as zip guide and coaster operator, that you add in one step.
Sell activities such as zipline tours, coaster rides, tubing sessions and skating, by time slot with places per slot or as a day pass. Set them up in Products and prices.

Sell has an Activities tab. Pick the attraction, day and time to see places left, then add guests. At checkout, tick that each rider meets the height, weight and age limits, and sign the waiver at the counter when the attraction needs one.

Guests can buy activities online: they pick a day, then a time, see the limits before paying, and get a link to sign the waiver afterward. Two people can never buy the last place at once, and a refund frees the place.

A gate can stand at an attraction. Activity tickets are let in only there, on their day, from 15 minutes before their time, and once, and the screen says why a ticket is refused. A lift ticket or pass can include an attraction.
The weekly report and Money show activity sales by attraction, and a sales tax can apply to activities only.

releases.title: New menus and Settings, patrol crews and kits, conditions on every report, staff injuries, lost and found

notes.text: Crews: under Patrol, People, Crews, set up the shifts your patrol runs again and again, such as a weekend day crew from 8:00 to 4:30 at the summit hut. Give each the days, the season, the days it does not run, how many patrollers it needs, the fewest it can run with, and the roles it must have (a hill captain at least a Leader, an EMT or higher).

Make the days: one button makes a crew's spots for the whole season as drafts, with its standing members put on first, each in their role. Publish a week, a month or the rest of the season at once from the Schedule.

Patrollers sign up for open spots under Shift cover. A role spot can only be taken by someone with the rank or certification it needs. The patrol director chooses whether sign-ups go straight on or wait for a schedule builder to approve them (Patrol settings).

The Schedule and the Crews page show each crew day as filled of needed: green when full, amber when short, red when below the fewest it can run with or missing a role. Select a day to call for extra patrollers on a storm day: the extra spots are published at once and everyone free that day is messaged.

On Thursday, the schedule builders get a message when a weekend crew is short, and open spots are posted to the shift cover conversation. On duty and the Schedule mark anyone not signed in 15 minutes after their shift starts.

Rotating teams: set up your patrol's teams (A team, B team) under Crews, Teams, and let them take turns on a crew, a new team each week or each day it runs. The team whose turn it is goes on the crew's spots first, and each crew day shows whose turn it is.

Every patrol report keeps the conditions at the time from your own records: the trail and whether it was groomed, the latest snow and weather readings, and the lift's status and any stop when a lift was involved. The report's Conditions answers are filled in from them for the patroller to check.

Who was told, on every report: management, the insurer, a parent or guardian, EMS, police or the owner, with how and when. It works with no signal, and the patrol director can require it, for example the insurer told on serious cases.

Rental gear on a case: find it by contract number, the item's number or the renter's name. The report keeps the binding setting, who set it and the last service, and the gear is held until the rental shop logs an inspection.
Rental gear involved in a patrol case is held for inspection: it shows in Service with the case number, and goes back on the rack only after an inspection is logged. Turn it off in Rentals, Settings.

Kits: trauma bags, packed toboggans and lift evacuation kits, each with its contents, quantities, expiry dates and how often it is checked. Scan a kit's QR label to check or restock it, with no signal if need be; supplies used on a case come off the kit; and one board shows which kits are ready. Optional seals sign off an unopened kit in one tap.

The staff injury register, under Staff and schedule, Injuries: work injuries with the fields of OSHA's Forms 300 and 301, patrol cases with a staff patient added automatically, and the year summary in the Form 300A layout. Only the owner and those the owner names can open it.

Lost and found, under Front desk: log what is handed in with a photo, take reports at the counter or on your website, see likely matches, tell the guest when it is found, and hand it back with an ID check.
Times follow your mountain's own time zone. A demo uses your own zone, the owner can set the zone in Account, and when you are somewhere else times show the mountain's zone, for example 10:15 AM MT.
Everything is now in US English: color, canceled, organization, inquiries, and Fahrenheit and inches first on patrol reports.

Partner passes: redeem Indy Pass days at the window by the Indy rules (two free days, then one at 25% off), with blackout dates for Indy Base, a daily limit, a photo ID check, online reservations for free days, and a visits report to check Indy's statement.

Claim files, a documentation score and a season risk report: one printable claim file from any case (the approved report, care, photos with fingerprints, conditions, rental gear, who was told, witnesses, the scene diagram and the audit trail), report completeness and timeliness on Today, and a counts-only season report for your broker. Insurers get a secure link with a passcode after a records release; it expires, can be stopped, and every opening is logged.

Witnesses can write their statement in their own words on their own phone from a link sent by text or email, or a QR code, and sign it; it arrives on the case untouched. The Report also has a scene diagram for the direction of travel, the point of impact and what was around.

Prospects in the platform console: the ski areas we sell to, who runs them, the sales pipeline with next steps and follow-ups due, a timeline of calls and emails, research imports and a spreadsheet download. Starts with 72 researched independent ski areas; Indy Pass resorts are left out.

Outreach in the platform console: start outreach to a person at a prospect, approve the first email (drafted for them), and five emails over 45 days then a quarterly update go from your own mailbox until they reply, bounce or choose not interested.

Pay over the season: on Billing, choose to pay the yearly price in six monthly payments, November to April, with nothing to pay May to October. Everything keeps working all year, and starting in the summer, the first payment is November 1. Resort now includes Assets and fleet and Messages, and Patrol costs the same as an add-on as on its own.

The website's home page is about half as long: the claim story comes straight after the headline, the day is six short tiles linking to each solution page, the roles and trust sections are folded in, prices are one row with a link to Pricing, five questions instead of eleven, and Book a walkthrough is the main button.

Pricing on the website: a season billing choice, guided setup packages (with a Guided setup request kind in Leads), a comparison showing Verdynt/OS takes no cut of online sales, and the Pricing questions updated for the new Resort and Patrol prices.

Head strike or possible head injury: a one-tap Yes, No or Not sure on the Care tab and the Report for injury and collision cases, required before submitting. It shows Yes already when a head injury is recorded on the Care tab. The Head injury questions on the Report open, and the Head check is marked due, only for Yes or Not sure; a neck injury now counts under Spine rather than Head.

On the patrol report, the Required and For approval tags now show only on fields that still need an answer, and they are smaller. A tag goes the moment the field is filled in or marked N/A, and comes back if it is cleared. Recommended fields no longer carry a tag.
The product website now leads with the patient care record that holds up later: a new page for owners and insurers, a free incident report review, and shorter feature lists.

The product website's header, menus and spacing are rebuilt: the header lines up with the page, Product opens a menu of every solution page, phones get a full-screen menu with the solutions grouped and the buttons kept at the bottom, tablets a menu that slides in from the right, and plan cards on Pricing line up.

The roadmap under Help, Coming to Verdynt/OS, is rebuilt from a full review of the app: first a busy Saturday that never waits (more room at peak, selling with no internet, sales tax by area, QuickBooks Online), then season pass payment plans and pass revenue over the season, signing in with your company login, guest pages anyone can use, labor cost and payroll, and your lift gates; later, groups of mountains, lift inspections by lift type, hiring, summer operations and Canada.

Signing out, by you or after 15 minutes, now starts the app over. A checkout, a customer, the Ask panel or anything else left open is closed, so the next person on a shared computer or tablet never sees it. A card already charged on the reader in an unfinished checkout goes back to the guest.
The Ask assistant forgets your conversation when you sign out, and a follow-up question only uses your own earlier questions.
A page that only refreshes itself, like a board or the Inbox count, no longer keeps you signed in. After an hour with nobody using it, the sign-in ends.

The patrol-room screen now shows only who is on duty. Nothing else opens on that tablet until the leader presses Leave this screen and confirms it is them, or presses Sign out. It stays signed in all day.
Pressing Sign out on a phone or tablet turns phone alerts off on it, so on a shared device the next person is never alerted for you. Turn them on again after you sign in.

Witnesses, responders, people in a collision and rental gear added to a case by mistake are now marked entered in error with a reason. They stay on the report, struck through, instead of being removed.
While a case is on legal hold, nothing on it can change except adding notes.

Only a patrol admin can change who reviews reports, the Patrol Director, and which kinds of case are reviewed. Group members can still change the reminder time. Every change is recorded with what it was before and after.
If you changed the review group in the last 30 days, your own reports go for review, whatever the kind of case.
Photo previews can only be added while a report can still be changed, and opening a preview is now recorded in the access log, like opening the original.
Insurer and broker links now show the original photo, the file whose fingerprint the report lists.

When a mountain leaves Verdynt/OS, nothing is deleted on its own. After the export window it is marked due for deletion, and deleting it is a deliberate step that is refused while any patrol case is on legal hold. Patrol reports, signed waivers, the audit trail and the OSHA injury log are always kept.
Program registrations, lesson payments and shop orders no longer turn away a guest who pays the same amount as someone else that day.

A guest who cancels a lesson request while still on the card payment page is never charged for nothing. The payment page closes, and any payment that gets through anyway is refunded in full and marked Refunded automatically.

A card payment online that cannot be matched to its order, request or registration is now refunded in full automatically instead of being kept. Every card payment also remembers which Stripe account it went to, so refunds always go back through the right account.

Refunding an order paid with more than one card now refunds each card, oldest first, never more than that card paid. A card taken on a separate card machine is left for the desk to refund on that machine.

Card reader payments are recorded even if the checkout screen is refreshed or loses its connection while the guest taps. Payments still waiting on the reader show under Billing, Card readers, with Check again and Cancel it.
If the reader does not answer in 3 minutes, a card that went through after all is added to the sale instead of being lost.

A Word, Excel or PowerPoint file too big to read safely is still saved and opens as normal. It shows Could not read the file and is found by its title. The same goes for photos or scanned pages over 40 megapixels and PDFs over 1,000 pages.
Sign-in lockouts now hold even when many guesses arrive at once: 10 wrong passwords, 5 wrong PINs or 5 wrong codes in a row lock that login for a while.

After 50 wrong codes in one day, signing in with an emailed code stops for that login. Sign in with your password and two-step, or a passkey, to turn it back on, or ask a manager to set a new password.
Signing in from a browser that cannot remember your device now asks for an emailed code, the same as any new device.

New menus. On a computer the menu is always open. Owners and managers see every app in five groups; everyone else sees a short menu for their job, such as Sell, Gate, Rentals, Customers, Waivers and Online shop at the ticket window. Every other app you may use is under All apps at the bottom, and Jump to still finds anything.

Each tab has its own address, so Back returns to the tab you were on, and refreshing or sharing a link opens the same tab. The top of every page shows where you are, such as Rentals / Service, with a Help button beside the title.

Account is now Settings, with its own list: your sign-in; the mountain's details, logins, shared computers, billing, card payments and the assistant; and a page for each app's setup. Change what you need, then press Save changes in the bar at the bottom.

Setup moved out of the apps and into Settings: gate devices, partner pass rules, online shop prices and limits, ski school levels and online booking, the public availability page, rental settings, waiver wording, staff setup, program settings and patrol setup. Managers get a settings button beside each app's title, such as Rentals settings, and for two weeks a short note shows where it went.
Owners can choose the menu each role sees under Settings, Team and logins, Menus for each role: which apps, their order, and the screen it opens on. Inbox and My shifts are always in.
On a phone, the bottom bar shows your first four apps and Menu, which opens everything as large tiles.
Screens follow your phone or computer's light or dark setting. Pick Light or Dark beside your name to change it on that device.
On a shared counter computer, Switch person at the bottom of the menu brings up the PIN screen for the next person.

Patrol has four sections in the menu while it is open: Now, Cases, People and Gear, each with its own tabs. Home is now called Board, and the Access log is a tab under Cases. Old Patrol links still open the right page.
Patrol settings, Report requirements and Access levels are under Settings, Patrol, opened from the Patrol settings button at the top of Patrol. Each shows to the same people as before.
Partner passes is now the last tab of Sell. A mountain that takes no partner pass, such as Indy Pass, can hide it under Settings, Sell and gate.

Today shows large job buttons for lift and mountain staff, instructors, the ticket window and patrol, such as Opening check, Report a problem, Today's lessons, Will-call pickups and New case. Report a problem opens a new work order straight away.
Card payments and card readers have their own page in Settings, Payments and card readers, and the online shop and lesson booking pages link straight to it when card payments are not set up yet.

releases.title: Patrol reports your patrol director sets the rules for

notes.text: Report requirements: under Patrol, Admin, the patrol director chooses what each kind of report must hold, and when. Each item is Off, Recommended, Required to approve or Required to submit, and can be limited to some cases: serious, transported, under 18, a collision, refused care, staff on duty, rental gear or a lift. Start from NSAA standard, Lean volunteer patrol or Insurer-ready (a draft), see every change before it is loaded, and adjust it. Mandatory fields set before are kept as they were.

In a report, each field shows Required, For approval or Recommended, each section says how many are left, and Next missing item goes straight to the next gap. A required field that cannot be answered can be marked N/A with a reason (declined, could not answer, left before it was asked), which the report shows instead of a blank.

Before the patient leaves (when the patrol director turns it on): recording an outcome, or stamping hand-off or transport, opens a short checklist for contact details, a parent or guardian for anyone under 18, the signed refusal, the rental number and witnesses. Each is done there and then or skipped with a reason. It works with no signal, never holds up care, and the reviewer sees every skip.

Reviewing: the review box lists what is missing for approval, every N/A answer and every skip. The Patrol Director can approve with an exception, with a reason for each missing item; other reviewers send it back. Exceptions, N/A answers and skips show on every copy of the report, including released copies. A report is always judged against the rules in force when it was submitted.

Signatures, witnesses and contact details can be taken with no signal: they wait on the phone, with the time they were taken, and are sent once when the signal returns. The refusal of care can be signed on a case started with no signal.

Website: the demo is described as built on the visitor's own mountain; the home page points patrol directors to the Patrol only plan and its price (read from the console's plans); the Patrol only card on Pricing lists what a patrol gets; a How switching works section on Pricing; "No card, no contract, your data exports any time" beside the buttons; the patrol page lists report requirements, the before-the-patient-leaves checklist, the report check, photo evidence, Locate caller and staff injury alerts.

releases.title: Starting a case with no signal, fixed

notes.text: Starting a case with no signal now always opens it. Before, if no case had been opened since the app was loaded, the new case showed an error instead. The report form's layout is now kept on the phone whenever Patrol is opened with a signal.
The red No connection banner no longer covers the top of an open window, such as New case.

releases.title: The ski area copy goes into the server image

notes.text: The server image now includes the data folder, so the demo page uses our own copy of the US ski areas instead of the busy public map servers. If the copy is missing, that is logged once.

releases.title: Demo mountains from our own copy of the ski area map

notes.text: The demo page now searches our own copy of every US ski area, built from OpenSkiData (OpenSkiMap.org, from OpenStreetMap) by scripts/ski-areas-build.js, instead of asking the public map servers, which are often too busy to answer. Without the file it falls back to the live lookup.

releases.title: Demo map lookup: more servers, and the reason when it fails

notes.text: Finding a mountain on the demo page now tries three public map servers instead of two, uses the plainest form of each map query, and logs exactly what each server said when none answers, so a failure can be traced.

releases.title: Demos built on the visitor's own mountain

notes.text: The demo page asks for the mountain's name and state, finds it on OpenStreetMap, and asks "Is this you?" with a drawing of its lifts and trails. The demo is then built on those real lift and trail names, centered on the real hill, in its time zone, with made-up prices, staff, guests and patrol cases. If the map has too little, or is not answering, the sample mountain is built as before.

releases.title: Sign in with a code from your email, and Forgot password?

notes.text: Sign in without a password: on the sign-in page, press Email me a code instead, then type the six-digit code or tap the link in the email. It works once, for 10 minutes. If you use a passkey or an authenticator app, you still do that step.
Forgot password? on the sign-in page: we email a code, you choose a new password, and you are signed in. Every other device is signed out, and you get an email saying the password changed.
Staff with an email on their login can now reset a forgotten password themselves, so managers set fewer temporary passwords. Add an email to a login in Account to give them this.

releases.title: Staff injuries, first step: who the patient is, and the owner is told

notes.text: At the top of each patient, choose Guest, Staff member on duty, Staff member off duty, or Volunteer on duty. Staff and volunteers hurt while working are not counted as guest injuries and never get the guest follow-up email.

When patrol marks a patient as staff, the owner and GM get an email straight away (and a text when texting is set up), with no injury details. If someone on duty goes to hospital, a second note gives OSHA's 8 and 24 hour deadlines. A volunteer is flagged for you to decide.
Patrol statistics show staff hurt on duty as their own figure, outside the guest rate per 1,000 visits and the activity, ability and helmet figures.
The roadmap in the app is now plain Now, Next and Later, with no dates.

releases.title: Patrol field kit: case photos, cases started with no signal, locating a caller, readings in checks

notes.text: Photos on a case: added at full size and kept exactly as taken, with a fingerprint recorded when added. When and where come from the photo itself. Open one to Verify it is unchanged or download the original; a wrong one is marked entered in error, never deleted.

Start a case with no signal: New case opens it on your phone straight away, with a patient to record on. Time stamps and bedside entries wait with it, and it all sends in order when the signal returns.

Locate caller, on a call in Dispatch: we text the caller a link, and when they tap it their phone's position appears on the call with how accurate it is. The guest help page can send the guest's position with the request too.

Gear checks ask for readings and dates: oxygen pressure, AED pads and battery, a trauma bag's earliest expiry. One outside its OK range or inside its warning fails the check and flags the item. Set the steps for each kind of gear under Gear, Equipment, Check steps.

Checklists can ask for a reading with its OK range (extinguisher pressure, battery volts) or a date that fails as it gets close. A reading outside the range fails the item by itself and opens a work order.
A case kept on the phone now also opens in a dead spot when the Patrol page itself has to be reloaded.

releases.title: Demo emails from Dan

notes.text: Everyone who starts a demo gets a welcome email from Dan (SITE_FOUNDER_NAME), replies to hello@: a link that signs them straight in for the life of the demo, three things to try first, and what Verdynt/OS is. The password is never emailed.

The daily job sends two follow-ups: on day 2 a note about one part they have not opened yet (with a link straight to it), and two days before the demo ends a note with the next steps. Nobody gets them after pressing the stop link or asking for a walkthrough or trial.
Console, Demos: an Emails column shows what each person was sent, and Send sign-in link emails a fresh link (older links stop working) for anyone who lost theirs.
Security: body-parser updated to 2.4.0 (a denial-of-service fix for compressed request bodies), so the deploy's package check passes.

releases.title: Fixes: the park map list, clearer assistant errors

notes.text: The daily park map no longer shows the word "null" under "Nothing is on the map for this day yet".
When the assistant cannot answer because of a problem on our side, it now says so plainly and points you to Help.
Console: the Assistant section shows the last error from Anthropic in plain words (out of credit, key not accepted, unknown model, busy), and every error is logged as job "assistant".

releases.title: The assistant: ask how to do anything, and Assistant Plus

notes.text: Ask, in the menu under Jump to, opens an assistant beside any screen. Ask in your own words and it answers from Help and your mountain's own setup, with buttons to the Help article and the screen. It explains and links; it never changes anything.
An answer that did not help has Ask support: your question, the answer and the screen go to Verdynt/OS support, who reply to your email.

Assistant Plus (add-on, $69 a month): staff can also ask about today's scans and sales, lessons, program days, lifts and trails, and who is working. It only looks up what that person's role can already see, and never patient care records.

With Assistant Plus, guests get a Questions button on the pages you choose (online shop, program registration, lesson booking, family page). It answers from your public information only, and what it cannot answer comes to your email with the guest's address to reply to. Set it up under Account, Assistant, where you can also see every question asked.
The Help article on taking payment now covers the card reader (Charge on reader) instead of saying cards are taken on a separate machine.
Console: each mountain shows the assistant's questions and cost this month against its cap, the ones not answered or passed on, and Change the cap.

Website: the assistant on the home page (guest pages, FAQ), Product (New this season, the Questions button page, Always there), Pricing (included with every plan, an Assistant Plus question) and Security (what it can and cannot see). The home page guest pages also gain Program registration and the Family page.

releases.title: Best-of-breed programs: your own types, season pass pricing, a family page

notes.text: Program types are your own: add, rename, hide and order them (Multi-week lessons, Race team, Homeschool...). Programs are grouped under them here and online.

A place is priced from parts: lessons, a lift ticket part that a season pass holder does not pay, and rental and a helmet when asked for. Online, a pass on file is found at once; if not, the child is marked to check at the first lesson, with Seen or No pass on the roster.
A season pass bought after registering, at the window or online: your choice in Program settings of nothing, a refund of the lift ticket part to the card, or a credit. The program ticket is voided.

Ski or snowboard for each child, days that are ski or snowboard only, and a snowboard minimum age. Classes can be the ski school's levels: preset from the report card, and the program shows on the report card.
Allergies, medical notes and who may pick up, asked at registration and shown on the roster and attendance sheet. Scan a child's program ticket to mark them here.

Rules for families: cancel online up to a number of days before the first lesson (less a fee), switch to a day with room, and whether late joiners pay for the lessons left. A reminder email the day before (meeting place, what to bring), and weather cancellations by text as well.

The family page at /family/your-mountain: parents sign in with an email link and see every child's dates, weather changes, attendance, class, lift ticket, balance and report card; they update allergies and pickup, switch day and cancel within your rules.
Selling a program place asks ski or snowboard, season pass, rental and helmet. Selling a season pass to a child in a program applies the mountain's refund or credit choice.

releases.title: Lesson programs in sessions: pick a weekday, makeup weeks for weather, online registration

notes.text: Programs run in sessions: set up Session 1 once (first week, number of weeks, makeup weeks, times, price and the weekdays it runs) and every day's lesson dates are made, each day its own group with its own spots and waitlist. Copy it to set up Session 2. Holidays you skip move the run on a week.

Weather: cancel one date, or every program lesson on a storm day. That group's makeup date becomes a lesson and families are emailed. When the makeup weeks are used up you see each family's share of one lesson, and can add a date.
Classes by level within each day: split on the first day, or preset from last session's class or the ability on file. Instructors take attendance from the lesson date.

Prices: early bird prices with an end date, a different price for one day, a sibling discount (percent or dollars) for the second and later child, and bundles that sell several sessions at one price. A program can include a lift ticket for every lesson (issued at no charge) and rental gear (the roster shows each child's sizes).

Parents register online at /programs/your-mountain: choose the session or bundle and the day, add each child, accept the waiver and pay by card. The confirmation email lists every lesson date and the makeup date. A full day offers its waitlist, and a day that fills while someone pays is refunded automatically.
Sell, Programs: choose the session and day (or a bundle) for programs run in sessions. Sibling discounts apply in the basket.

releases.title: Email us: hello@ and support@runmyresort.com

notes.text: Help now gives owners and managers an address for Verdynt/OS support: support@runmyresort.com. Say what you were doing and include the version number shown at the bottom of Help.

The website shows hello@runmyresort.com for sales and questions and support@runmyresort.com for customers (footer, Contact, Privacy, Terms, Security, and the company details search engines read), and serves /.well-known/security.txt. Contact page requests and replies to Verdynt/OS's own emails go to hello@. SITE_HELLO_EMAIL, SITE_SUPPORT_EMAIL and SITE_CONTACT_EMAIL change them.

releases.title: A second look before you submit, fill-in from the story, and a clearer Patrol menu

notes.text: Before a patient care report is submitted, Verdynt/OS points out gaps a reviewer would notice: a head injury without AVPU or GCS, a splint without CMS before and after, oxygen without the flow, a medication without its effect, abnormal last vitals with no repeat set, times out of order, or words like "drunk" or "his fault" in the narrative. Each one links straight to the field and says why it matters. They are suggestions only: fix them, or submit anyway. The review group sees the same list.

Speak the story: tap the microphone on your phone's keyboard in the narrative box. Where the mountain has turned it on, Fill in from the story suggests answers for the empty fields (helmet, lost consciousness, activity and more), each with the words it came from. Nothing is saved until you tick it.

The Patrol menu is easier to find your way around: five groups (Now, Cases, People, Gear, Admin) with clearer names, every page visible on a phone without scrolling sideways, bigger buttons for gloved hands, and New case always at the top.

Fill in from the story needs PATROL_AI=on and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (optional PATROL_AI_MODEL). The narrative is sent to the AI provider, so set these only once a business associate agreement is in place; each mountain then turns it on in Patrol, Settings.

releases.title: A map of your pipes, valves and equipment, and a satellite view on every map

notes.text: Assets and fleet has a Map: put valves, hydrants, pumps, pump houses and transformers on it as points, snowmaking water and air lines, power, sewer and fibre runs as lines, and ponds and buildings as areas. Each system has its own color and can be switched on and off. Place things with your phone's location, tap the map, or record a pipe run by walking it. Tie a point to an asset in the register, and its page links straight to it. Managers can download the whole map for GIS software or a contractor.
Every map (patrol, terrain park and assets) now has a Satellite view of the ground, and zooms in further, close enough to place a single valve.

Map settings: the satellite layer is the USGS National Map's aerial imagery by default (free, public domain, US only). MAP_IMAGERY_URL and MAP_IMAGERY_ATTRIBUTION swap in a paid provider, MAP_IMAGERY_MAX_ZOOM sets its deepest tile level (default 16), and MAP_MAX_ZOOM how far every map zooms (default 21).

releases.title: Guides, checklists and search improvements on the website

notes.text: A Resources section on the website with free, printable guides for ski areas: a chairlift daily inspection checklist, a terrain park inspection checklist, how to write an incident report, and how to choose ski area software. Each is marked up as an article for Google.
An About page, and the LinkedIn company page linked from the footer and in the structured data once SITE_SAME_AS is set.
The home page heading now carries "Ski area management software", page addresses in capitals redirect to the lowercase page, and Cloudflare Web Analytics is allowed on the website (not in the app).

releases.title: Four new website pages for search

notes.text: Four new website pages, each written for a search ski area managers make: Ski area POS, Online lift ticket sales, Terrain park software and Ski area staff scheduling. Each has its own title, description, questions and answers for Google, and is in the menu, the footer, the sitemap and llms.txt.
Shorter search titles on the ski patrol, lift ticket and ski school pages, so Google shows them whole. The product page links to each new page and mentions the card reader.

releases.title: Card reader, lesson canceling, pin dropping, your own guest types

notes.text: Take cards on a Stripe smart reader at the ticket window. Pair a reader under Billing, then choose Charge on reader at checkout: the guest taps, inserts or swipes, and the money goes straight into your own Stripe account. Refunds work the same as online card payments. If the sale is closed before it finishes, the reader payment is refunded for you.

Cancel a lesson, or every lesson on a storm day. Package lessons get their credit back, lessons paid online are refunded in full to the card, counter sales are listed for a refund at the desk, and every booked guest gets one email. A lesson added by mistake with nobody booked can be deleted instead.

Dropping feature pins in the terrain park waits for a good GPS fix and shows how close it is, drops the pin by itself once the fix is good, and lets you drag it into place. Walk the park drops one feature after another as you reach each one. Each pin shows how it was placed.

Your own guest types, under Products and prices, Guest types. Add types like College or Local, rename them, set the ages that pick them online, hide them and change their order. Your current Adult, Youth, Child, Senior and Military prices carry straight over.

Day by day, under Mountain status, Snow and weather: each finished day is written down every night with the weather at the mountain, new snow, whether you were open, visits, tickets, lessons and revenue. Fill in the past year with one button. This is the history the visitor forecast will learn from.
On a phone, buttons in a list no longer break their words across two lines.

releases.title: Demo sign-ups confirm their email

notes.text: The try page emails a 6-digit code before it builds a demo, so every demo lead is a real address. Codes last 15 minutes, only the newest works, five wrong tries use it up, and throwaway inboxes are turned away. On in production and staging whenever email is set up; TRY_EMAIL_CHECK=off turns it off.

releases.title: Demo mountains on staging

notes.text: Demo mountains can be built on staging again: the demo builder's own internal requests were being stopped by the staging password page.

releases.title: Verdynt/OS: a new name and a new look

notes.text: DAY/OS is now Verdynt/OS, with a new logo and a dark slate and gold look. Prefer the light look? Choose Light in the account menu. Printing always stays light.
Adding Verdynt/OS to a phone's home screen works again, with the new icon.

releases.title: Every release is checked on staging first

notes.text: Coming to DAY/OS in Help now lists data import from your old system and the new assistants: the snow report, the morning brief, patrol report checks, asking your data and documents, and suggested guest replies.

Staging: a private test copy with its own database, Stripe in test mode, email to the team only and a shared password. deploy.sh now puts a release on staging; promote.sh puts that exact build live after a typed confirmation.

releases.title: See what's coming

notes.text: Help now has Coming to DAY/OS: what we're building now, next and later. Tell us what your mountain needs most and it moves up the list.

releases.title: Faster schedule pickers

notes.text: Choosing who to put on a shift is quicker for a big crew: everyone's availability, training and clashes are now checked several people at a time.
The patrol schedule's who-can-take-this list and the open shifts page load faster on a big roster.
Code sweep: package updates (no known vulnerabilities), unused code removed, patrol access checks for a whole roster in one query, and a smaller container image.

releases.title: Guest payments go to your own Stripe account

notes.text: Guests' card payments (the online shop, lesson payments, date changes and patrol giving) now go straight into your mountain's own Stripe account, and Stripe pays them out to your bank. Connect it under Billing, Guest card payments. Card payments open as soon as Stripe has what it needs.
Billing shows whether guest card payments are on, which Stripe account they go to, and whether payouts are set up. Only the owner can connect or disconnect the account, after confirming it is them.

Stripe Connect: each mountain's guest payments are direct charges on its own Standard account. The console shows each mountain's connection and can set a DAY/OS fee per mountain (a share and a fixed amount, 0 unless set), kept by Stripe and returned in proportion on refunds; gifts never carry it. Events from a mountain's account only ever count for that mountain. Set up the Connect webhook as DEPLOY.md, Guest card payments, describes.

releases.title: The new DAY/OS logo

notes.text: DAY/OS has a new logo: day/os with a mountain peak for the slash. It is on the sign-in screen, at the top of the menu, and as the app icon when you add DAY/OS to a phone's home screen.
The website uses the new logo in its header and footer, its browser icon and its link preview image. The logo files, for light and dark backgrounds, are in public/brand.

releases.title: A faster, phone-first website

notes.text: The runmyresort.com website is rebuilt for phones: a sticky header, a full-screen menu, a Try the demo and Book a walkthrough bar at the bottom, long feature lists folded behind "What it does", and rows that swipe sideways. Home is about half as long on a phone.

Six pages written for what ski areas search for: ski patrol, lift tickets and passes, ski school, ski rentals, online waivers, and lift and fleet maintenance. Each has its own title, questions and links, and is in the sitemap, the menu and the footer.

Search engines now see the live plans and prices in Home and Pricing, richer structured data on every page, and /llms.txt, a plain summary for AI assistants. The website's styles and script are kept by browsers for a year and refreshed by each release.
The Patrol only plan on Pricing listed "Everything in Resort, plus" with nothing under it. It now lists its own apps.

releases.title: SummitOps is now DAY/OS

notes.text: SummitOps is now called DAY/OS, the operating system for your day. Nothing else changes: your sign-in, your data and every app work as before. The website moves to runmyresort.com.
The website, emails, the app, the console and the link preview image all use the new name. Set the runmyresort.com addresses on the service as DEPLOY.md, Putting the website live, describes.

releases.title: Patrol on its own

notes.text: A Patrol only plan, for a ski patrol that signs up on its own: Patrol and Documents, $149 a month or $1,500 a year. It is on the website's Pricing page, and the Ski patrol page and Contact form take patrol sign-ups.
Runs and lifts in Patrol settings: a patrol without the Lifts and trails app keeps its own list, which cases, trail checks and sweep routes point at.
Import the patrol roster from a spreadsheet (Team, Import from a spreadsheet). People already on the roster are skipped, and leaders and directors are set by hand.

A free read-only login for the ski area (Account, Logins, role Ski area): the patrol's day in numbers and every approved report, nothing else. It uses two-step sign-in and every report it opens is recorded.
On the Patrol only plan, signing in opens Patrol, and the menu shows only what a patrol uses.

releases.title: Passkeys and tiered sign-in

notes.text: Passkeys: sign in with your fingerprint, face or your device's PIN instead of a password and code. Nobody can phish or guess a passkey. Add one in Account, then press "Sign in with a passkey". A passkey also counts as two-step sign-in.

Before sensitive actions you are asked to confirm it is you, even when signed in: refunds over $200, changing someone's role or password, switching a login off, downloading customer, waiver or patient lists, releasing a patient record, changing billing, and weakening sign-in rules. It lasts 10 minutes, and straight after signing in counts.

Account shows where you are signed in and the devices you have used, so you can sign out anywhere else. A sign-in from a new device is emailed to you; without two-step sign-in, a code is emailed first.

Shared terminals: enroll the ticket window, rental counter or other shared computers in Account. Counter, instructor and lift staff then switch in with their username and a personal PIN, so nobody shares a login. A terminal's sign-in ends after 15 minutes unused.
Season end: set the last day of the season under Logins, and seasonal logins stop working after it (owners and managers are never affected). Change one person's date in Edit to bring them back.

Patrollers will need two-step sign-in (a passkey takes a minute), because Patrol holds patient details. Mountains already on SummitOps have two weeks; you will see a reminder until then. Patrol Admins and Managers need it now.
New passwords must be at least 12 characters and must not contain your username, email name or the mountain's name. A short phrase of a few words is easiest.
Console: operators can add passkeys (then they sign in with the passkey only), and changing a mountain now needs it opened first with a reason, for up to 8 hours, recorded in its history.

releases.title: Security hardening

notes.text: Signing out now ends the session on the server, so a copy of the sign-in kept on another device stops working too. A session left unused for an hour ends, and changing your password signs you out everywhere else. Everyone signs in again once after this update.
Ten wrong passwords in a row lock that login for 15 minutes, and a password already exposed in a data breach elsewhere can no longer be chosen.
Owners and managers must set up two-step sign-in. You are taken to set it up the next time you sign in; it takes a minute with an authenticator app.
Reports and notes saved on a phone while offline are now locked with a key tied to your login, kept separately for each person, and cannot be read once you sign out.
Uploaded files are checked to be what their name says. Zip files and Office files with macros are no longer accepted.

Close mountain in the console: the mountain is paused and everyone signed out at once, and everything in it is deleted after the export window (60 days unless you choose). Resuming it before then cancels the deletion.

The platform key turns itself off once an operator has two-step sign-in. Console actions and sign-ins are also written to Cloud Logging. The daily job now clears website requests older than two years and old sign-in records.

A one-time security setup script for Google Cloud (bash scripts/harden.sh) and an optional web firewall (bash scripts/cloud-armor.sh). Deploys now stop if a package has a known serious security problem.

releases.title: The morning board on Today

notes.text: Today now opens with the morning board: every lift with why it is open, on hold or cannot open; patrollers on duty and runs checked, with any run on hold and why; tonight's grooming; machines and lifts due for service; and unfilled shifts, open work orders and open incidents. Press any heading or number to open that page. If you chose your own tiles before, add it with Customize.

releases.title: Website search engine setup and a ski patrol page

notes.text: The website is set up for search engines: titles and descriptions for what ski areas search for, one address per page, link previews, a sitemap, and structured data with your live prices and each page's questions. The app and console stay out of search results.
A Ski patrol page on the website, for patrol directors, linked from the menu. Set GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION to prove the website to Google Search Console.

releases.title: The product website goes live

notes.text: The product website is now part of SummitOps: Home, Product, Pricing, Security, Contact, Privacy and Terms, updated with patrol operations, billing, RFID and the Inbox. It is at /site everywhere, and at the top of its own domain once SITE_HOSTS is set.
Pricing on the website comes from the console's Plans and prices, so changing a price there changes the website. The launch plans and add-ons are added for you.
Console: Leads lists walkthrough and trial requests from the Contact page, with status, notes and Make their mountain. Each is also emailed to SITE_CONTACT_EMAIL.

releases.title: Billing, and printing fixed

notes.text: Billing: choose your SummitOps plan, add-ons and monthly or yearly, and pay by card, US bank account or emailed invoice. Manage payment changes the card, shows receipts or cancels. New mountains start with a 14-day free trial.

If a payment fails or the trial ends, everything keeps working for 14 days with a notice at the top. After that SummitOps is read only until paid; patrol, the time clock and the Inbox always keep working.
Printing works again: the hand-off report, take-home instructions, refusal form and other patrol printouts were coming out blank.
Console: Plans and prices (with Sync to Stripe), a Billing column on the mountain list, and Change billing on each mountain for trials, free mountains and payments taken by check.

releases.title: Patrol operations, and fixes from an EMS review

notes.text: On duty: patrollers sign in when they reach the patrol room and out when they leave, on their phone or a shared patrol-room tablet. Dispatch now lists volunteers as well as paid patrollers, with their radio and station.
Phone alerts: turn them on for each phone, and you are alerted when dispatch sends you to a call, with On my way to answer. Critical calls alert everyone on duty, and can text responders too.

Closing sweep: set up routes of lifts and runs, give each to someone on duty, mark each stop as it is swept, call in anyone found, and call the mountain clear with the time. A late sweep raises an alert.

Opening checks: check each run (hazards marked, ropes and signs, padding) before opening it, or hold or close it with a reason. Mountain status updates at once, and runs now have a Hold status and a closure reason.

Medications: a formulary set by the medical director (authority, routes, largest dose, who may give it), stock by lot and expiry taken from as doses are given, controlled counts, and oxygen pressure and AED pad, battery and download tracking.

Giving a medication now checks the patient's allergies, and for nitroglycerin a recent blood pressure of at least 100 and no erectile dysfunction medication. Each patroller has a medical certification on the roster.
Tourniquet and pelvic binder treatments. A tourniquet's time shows at the top of the patient and of the hand-off sheet.

The hand-off sheet puts time-critical items first (tourniquet, stroke with last known well, cardiac arrest), then follows the MIST order, and now includes the primary survey, spinal motion restriction, and drugs or alcohol.

Reports check more before they are submitted: a head injury with loss of consciousness, amnesia or a low GCS does not go back to skiing without a written refusal or a named clearance; a refusal with drugs, alcohol or head injury signs needs a note on capacity; serious and transported patients need vitals.
Times in the future (23:45 typed for 13:45) are refused, and the vitals reminder stops once a patient has an outcome or is handed off.
Lost-person search on a case: who is missing and where last seen, search areas assigned to patrollers (who are alerted) and marked searched, and when and where they were found.
Checklists for a patroller or employee injured or exposed on duty, and for lift-related incidents (including notifying the state tramway inspector).
Daily log: one page per day built from everything recorded, with the leaders' notes, a sign-off, addenda after it, and search.
Lift evacuation: each lift's plan, equipment and patrollers needed, who on duty is ready, and drills that add a training record for each patroller.
Volunteer days: set the season's minimum, and each patroller sees their progress; reminders go to anyone short. Patrollers can be allowed to take open shifts themselves on Team, Cover.
Avalanche work, for mountains that turn it on: snow and hazard observations, and control shots by slide path with results, which can hold or close the run.
Records requests: log who asked for a report and on what authority, and release the approved report with a release number and a printable release pack. Cases can be put on legal hold.
Patrol settings: the medical director and protocol version, stamped on each report at sign-off, and the settings for the features above.
No signal: the last cases you opened can still be opened on your phone for 12 hours, and a new case started with no signal is sent when the signal returns.
Days patrolled now count the days people signed in on duty, and show each volunteer's days against the minimum.

releases.title: Patrol access from the staff page

notes.text: Edit details on a patroller’s staff page now has their patrol rank and patrol access level, so owners and managers can change them without going into Patrol.
Edit on the patrol roster always shows the access level. Patrol Admins, owners and managers can change it; everyone else sees who can.
The Needs staff housing option is gone from adding and editing staff.

releases.title: Shift cover for ski patrol

notes.text: Can’t make a patrol shift? Ask for cover on Patrol, Team, Cover. Everyone on the roster sees it there and in the Patrol shift cover conversation in the Inbox, and anyone free at that time can take it. The shift moves to them and you both get a message.
Those who build the patrol schedule can choose to approve each swap first. Taking a shift then sends an offer, and the shift moves once it is approved.
Shifts waiting for cover are marked Needs cover on the patrol schedule. Putting someone else on one from the schedule counts as covered.

releases.title: Patrollers from the staff page, and patrol permissions

notes.text: Add everyone on the staff page, as an employee or a volunteer. Tick On ski patrol, or press Put on ski patrol on their staff page, and they appear in Patrol.
Create login right from a person’s staff page, with a username filled in from their name and a temporary password.
Anyone on the patrol roster with a login can open Patrol, whatever their login role, so staff who also patrol no longer need a separate patrol login.
Patrol Admins can give one patroller extra permissions, or take one away, without changing everyone at the same access level (Team, Permissions).
The staff list shows who is a volunteer and who is on ski patrol, with a filter for each. Volunteers stay off the time clock and payroll.

releases.title: Sign in with a username

notes.text: Sign in with your username or your email. Everyone now has a username (you can change yours on Account), and your email still works if you have one.
Logins no longer need an email, except for owners and managers, so volunteers and seasonal staff can have their own sign-in.
Forgot your password? A manager sets a temporary one and tells you; you choose your own the next time you sign in.
Owner and manager password resets from the console can be temporary too. Existing logins were given usernames by the migration (first initial and last name, or the email before the @).

releases.title: Patrol keeps its own roster and schedule

notes.text: Patrol has its own schedule (Team, Schedule): a weekly grid of the roster, built and published by the patrol director and leads. Volunteers and paid patrollers are both scheduled here, and publishing messages each patroller their shifts.
Add patrollers straight to the roster, volunteers included, without a staff record. Paid patrollers can be on the staff list too, for pay and the time clock.
Days patrolled: each person’s days and hours this season, with a download for volunteer credit.
Today’s posts now lists who is on the patrol schedule for the day.

Staff and schedule shows patrol coverage in a read-only Patrol row; patrol shifts are made in Patrol. A paid patroller’s patrol time counts toward their hours, and they cannot be booked on a work shift and patrol at the same time.
My shifts shows your published patrol shifts alongside your work shifts.
The migration moves upcoming patrol shifts from Staff and schedule into the new patrol schedule and cancels the originals with a note; past ones stay as history.

releases.title: A better Staff and schedule

notes.text: The schedule is now a weekly grid: people down the side, days across, unfilled shifts in their own row, and each person’s hours for the week. On a phone it shows one day at a time.

Click any shift to change its time, position, person or note. When choosing who works it, the people who can work it come first with their hours that week, and anyone who cannot is listed with the reason.
Copy last week, or save a typical week as a template and apply it to any week. People are kept only where they can still work the shift.
When your manager publishes the schedule, you get a message in your Inbox listing your shifts, and another if one of your published shifts changes or is canceled.
Hours: fix a missed clock-out or a wrong punch (with a reason, kept in the audit log), add a forgotten punch, approve the week, and export hours for payroll with overtime over 40 hours.
Each staff member has their own page: what they work as, certifications, availability, their login, their patrol and ski school roles, hours this week and upcoming shifts.
Staffing needs counts pass holders as well as tickets sold, and counts only filled shifts as covered.
Dates an instructor marks open on Instructor availability now count as available when scheduling, and someone who stops working comes off their future shifts automatically.
Opening someone’s availability, or a position’s required certifications, and saving no longer wipes what was saved. Both now open with what is saved.
Your availability in My shifts opens with what you saved before, and clocking in links your punch to the shift you are working.

releases.title: Version numbers and What's new

notes.text: SummitOps now has a version number, shown in Help and in your account menu, so you can tell at a glance which version you are using.
Help has a What's new page listing each update. Only the changes for your role and your mountain's apps are shown, and a small badge on Help tells you when there is something new.
The console shows the version that is live and every version that has been deployed, with when it first started and who deployed it.

deploy.sh says which version it is replacing, refuses to put an older version over a newer one (bash deploy.sh --allow-older to do it anyway), and checks that the new version is the one answering afterwards.

releases.title: Inbox and case review

notes.text: Inbox: send messages to one person or a group at your mountain, with links that open a customer, an order, a work order, a waiver, a document, an asset or a patrol case. Each person sees only the links their role can open.
A Share button on records sends a link to that record to someone in the Inbox.

Case review: when a patroller signs off a case, it goes to the review group (the Patrol Director and named backups), who approve it, send it back with comments or escalate it. The group chooses which kinds of case it reviews and gets a reminder after 72 hours.

releases.title: RFID cards and the injury network

notes.text: Gate: RFID cards. Load a pass onto a card, move it to a new card, and block a lost one. Cards are read by desk readers, by phone (NFC) or by camera.
Paired gates, turnstiles and handhelds check passes online and keep working from an offline list when the connection drops.
Two gates can no longer both let the same single-use ticket through, and a blocked card is always refused.
Injury network: mountains can choose to share de-identified injury counts and compare their numbers with similar mountains.
Guided tours walk new demo mountains through selling, the gate, patrol and more. The console has the network injury report.

releases.title: Waivers, the new case page, and assets

notes.text: Waivers: guests sign on a phone or tablet, with guardians for minors. You can look up who has signed, and every signed copy keeps the exact wording it was signed against.
A new patrol case page, with Care, Report and Record views, assessment tools, vitals, oxygen, medications, refusal and hand-off signatures. It saves on the phone when there is no signal.
Assets and fleet: one register for vehicles, lifts, snowmaking and buildings, with meters, fuel, inspections, service plans, parts, purchase orders, costs and QR labels.
Many small fixes and safety improvements from a full review of the app.
The database moved to Cloud SQL. Console operators sign in with their own email, password and authenticator, and the Demos page shows usage and lets you delete demos.
